extracted.intended_audience: researchers, peer reviewers, journal editors, and research-publishing stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A summary of evaluative criteria, expectations, and desired improvements for scholarly peer review drawn from a 2019 survey of researchers; covers what reviewers prioritize when assessing papers and what researchers want from review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to detect plagiarism or fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should reliably determine plagiarism or fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey finding: under half of researchers think peer review is currently able to reliably determine plagiarism or fraud — i.e., detecting misconduct is an expected function but perceived as inadequately performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper acknowledgement of previous work
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should ensure previous work is properly acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey finding: under half of researchers think peer review currently ensures prior work is properly acknowledged, indicating this is an expectation reviewers are judged against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper presents original research and novel contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by respondents as a top priority when assessing paper quality ('Originality and novelty'). Use to judge the contribution's uniqueness and advancement of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the study design and methods are appropriate and robust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly prioritized by reviewers ('Methodological soundness'). Includes checking experimental design, controls, sample size rationale, and appropriateness of methods for the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the manuscript is clearly and effectively communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers prioritize clarity ('Clarity of writing'); poor clarity can obscure strengths or weaknesses and should be flagged for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance/impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge the importance of the questions addressed and the potential impact of the findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey respondents list 'Importance/impact' as a key criterion — consider relevance to the field, potential to change practice or understanding, and audience interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the methods and reporting allow others to reproduce the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named by reviewers as a priority ('Reproducibility'). Includes availability of data, materials, protocols, and sufficient methodological detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the appropriateness and correctness of statistical analyses and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey lists 'Statistical validity' as a reviewer priority — reviewers should evaluate choice of tests, assumptions, effect sizes, confidence intervals, multiple testing corrections, and whether conclusions are supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the research complies with ethical standards (e.g., human/animal subjects, conflicts of interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in reviewers' priorities ('Ethical conduct') — includes checking approvals, consent, participant protection, and disclosure of conflicts/funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall trust and satisfaction in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of researchers' trust in and satisfaction with peer review processes and outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey metrics: 75% satisfied with peer review (up from 69% in 2009); 62% trusted the output they assessed a week before the survey; 37% were unsure they could trust output quality. Use as an outcome metric for system performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of guidance for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether clear guidance exists on how to conduct peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 56% of respondents believe there is a lack of guidance on how to review — indicates a standard that journals/publishers should provide reviewer guidance, checklists, or mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal reviewer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of structured training to improve review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 68% agree formal training would improve review quality. Recommendation-level criterion: implement consistent training programs or resources for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and credit for reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems to acknowledge and reward peer review labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers want better recognition for reviewing — e.g., formal credit, acknowledgement, or incentives to sustain volunteer reviewer contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faster turnaround times
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness of the review process from submission to decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers express desire for faster turnaround times; speed is a process-quality metric balancing thoroughness and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which review procedures and decisions are open and explainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey respondents want more transparent processes (e.g., clearer editorial criteria, decision rationales). Transparency is linked to trust and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review options
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of models where reviewer identities or reports are open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents expressed interest in open peer review options — could include signed reviews, published review reports, or open commentary mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public review reports for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing reviewers' reports alongside accepted articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers want public review reports for accepted papers as a transparency and accountability measure; this can serve as additional information for readers and validators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance for volunteer reviewer labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms to assure review quality given reliance on volunteers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication from the survey: the system relies heavily on volunteer labor without clear QA mechanisms. Standards could include editorial oversight, reviewer performance feedback, and cross-review checks.
